correctness.rationale: Two-point formula follows directly from commutativity and equality of squares. If all noncommuting pairs share a square, a noncommuting pair generates Q8: c=a²=b²=(ab)²=(ba)², ba=c^{-1}ab, and c²=1 with c nontrivial. The triple {1,a,b} has 6 products/7 quotients. The finite abelian decomposition reduces remaining nonexceptional cases to an element of order >=6 or C3²,C5²,C4×C2, each with an explicit 3-point witness. Exceptional groups balance all subsets by inversion or pigeonhole. The accompanying full exact finite verifier returned VERIFY_OK. No finite enumeration is used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The all-subsets balance condition is the extreme B(G)=2^{|G|} boundary of a central random-subset statistic in recent finite-group additive number theory. A complete structural classification of this boundary, plus the optimal constant three detection theorem and intrinsic sharp two-point criterion, separates global balance from high-probability statistical balance. Explicit quaternion and abelian obstruction families explain the structure. It does not claim a paper-sized contribution, distribution counts, or independence.
